top.line: One sentence as the whole offer: six promises, their proof, and three designs for a site built on it.
top.para: Six promises, just say it, stop renting.

in-short.line: Six promises with proof; three designs in different orders and voices; a recommendation.

sentence.line: The pitch says what the website cell is with no jargon, each clause answering a real complaint.

promises.line: Looks better, you own it, no lock-in, almost nothing to attack, costs once, change it by talking to Claude.

designs.line: Three sites by a designer agent: the order is the message.

examples.line: Yiheng Wang, Silvio Switha, José Bota and an invented orange grower, four looks from one team.

recommend.line: Six promises on the home page; just say it for technologists; stop renting for people on platforms.

limits.line: Mock-ups; an illustrative conversation; nothing sold; a vendor's figure.

sources.line: The static article, the designer agent's mock-ups, the example sites and Patchstack.
